claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous, primarily fcc, almost-equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
The as-cast or rapidly quenched starting alloy exhibits soft ferromagnetism and low coercivity.
Aging near 500°C for approximately 2 hours followed by controlled cooling will promote nanoscale precipitation.
An inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during aging.
Controlled cooling will avoid precipitate coarsening.
The aging treatment will form fine, coherent nanoprecipitates within the fcc matrix.
The nanoprecipitates will have higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the matrix.
The nanoprecipitates will act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Domain-wall pinning by the precipitates will increase the energy barrier for magnetization reversal.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will minimize the reduction in saturation magnetization.
The aged alloy will have greater coercivity than the corresponding as-cast or rapidly quenched baseline.
Aging may cause a slight change in saturation magnetization.
The aged alloy will shift from a soft-ferromagnetic response toward harder magnetic behavior.
The coercivity benefit is limited to a narrow aging-temperature and aging-time window.
Significantly higher aging temperatures or longer aging durations may produce coarse precipitates or complete phase separation.
Coarse precipitation or complete phase separation may degrade magnetic performance.

contradictions.description: The intervention is said to promote precipitation without degrading the overall single-phase structure, but formation of precipitates embedded in a matrix necessarily introduces at least a second distinguishable phase or compositional region.
